info.title: API.SH: Binance
info.description: The Binance API from API.SH: public Binance data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Binance announcements by category (new listings, delistings, news, activities, maintenance, API updates, airdrops): id, code, title, category, publish time and link, with the category totals; `code` (or an announcement link) returns one announcement with its full text. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-announcements

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category (default new_listings).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only titles containing this text.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: An announcement code or link, for its full text.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page (1-50, default 20).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Trading rules of one or more spot pairs: status, base and quote asset and precision, allowed order types, spot/margin flags, tick size, min/max price, step size, min/max quantity, min/max notional, permission sets and every filter as given, plus the exchange's rate limits and server time.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-exchange-info

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair. Required unless `symbols` is given.

parameters.name: symbols
parameters.description: Up to 100 comma-separated pairs.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Funding rate history of a Binance perpetual futures contract (USDⓈ-M by default, or COIN-M): each funding time with the rate (and in percent) and mark price, newest first, the average rate, plus the current mark and index price, last funding rate, interest rate and next funding time. Narrow with start and end.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-funding-rate

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: A futures symbol such as BTCUSDT (COIN-M: BTCUSD_PERP).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: usdm (default) or coinm.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of funding records (1-1000, default 100).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start time (ISO date or epoch).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End time (ISO date or epoch).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
OHLCV candlesticks for a spot pair: open time, open, high, low, close, base volume, close time, quote volume, trade count, taker-buy base and quote volume. Up to 1,000 candles per call between optional `start` and `end`. To page forward, pass `next_start` back as `start`; null when the range is done. With `market=usdm|coinm`, futures candles, and with `price_type=mark|index`, mark-price or index-price candles.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-klines

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair symbol, e.g. `BTCUSDT`, `ETHBTC` (a slash, dash or underscore between the assets is accepted).

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Candle size (default 1d).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start time: ISO date/time or unix seconds/milliseconds.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End time: ISO date/time or unix seconds/milliseconds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Candles per call, 1-1000 (default 500).

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: UTC offset that sets where day/week/month candles start, e.g. `+5:30` or `-8` (default UTC).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: `spot` (default), `usdm` (USDⓈ-M futures; `futures` also works) or `coinm` (COIN-M futures, e.g. `BTCUSD` or `BTCUSD_PERP`). Futures allow up to 1,500 candles per call; `timezone` and the `1s` interval are spot only.

parameters.name: price_type
parameters.description: Futures only: `last` (default, traded price with volumes), `mark` (mark price) or `index` (index price of the underlying pair). Mark and index candles have null volume fields. The answer then adds `market` and `price_type`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Every spot market on Binance with 24 h statistics: base and quote asset with names, last, open, high and low price, percent change, base and quote volume, circulating supply and market cap, tick size, minimum trade amount and the site's tags (e.g. Layer1_Layer2, Meme, AI, defi). Filter by quote asset, tag, text and minimum quote volume; sort by quote volume, change, market cap, price or symbol. `tags` lists the tags present in the result. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-markets

parameters.name: quote
parameters.description: Quote asset, e.g. USDT, USDC, BTC, FDUSD, EUR, TRY.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Site tag, e.g. `Layer1_Layer2`, `Meme`, `defi`, `AI`, `Gaming`, `pos` (see `tags` in a response).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text in the symbol or the base asset's name.

parameters.name: min_quote_volume
parameters.description: Only markets with at least this 24 h quote volume.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: TRADING (default), BREAK or ALL.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: quote_volume (default), change (biggest gain first), change_asc (biggest loss first), market_cap, price or symbol.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1). Pass `next_page` from the previous response.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Markets per page, 1-500 (default 100).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Binance top gainers, losers and volume leaders
get.description:
The biggest 24 h gainers, losers or volume leaders among Binance spot markets, ranked, with the same fields as /binance/v1/markets. Filter by quote asset and tag; markets under `min_quote_volume` (default 10,000) are left out so illiquid pairs do not dominate.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-movers

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: gainers (default), losers or volume.

parameters.name: quote
parameters.description: Quote asset, e.g. USDT.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Site tag, e.g. `Meme`.

parameters.name: min_quote_volume
parameters.description: Minimum 24 h quote volume (default 10000).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Markets, 1-200 (default 20).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Open interest of a Binance futures contract now, and its history for about the last 30 days at the chosen period (open interest in contracts and its value).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-open-interest

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: A futures symbol such as BTCUSDT (COIN-M: BTCUSD_PERP).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: usdm (default) or coinm.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: History interval (default 1h).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of history points (1-500, default 30).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.history_note: History covers about the last 30 days.

get.description:
The order book of a spot pair: bids and asks (price and quantity) to the chosen depth, best bid and ask, spread, mid price, total quantity on each side and the book's update id.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-orderbook

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair symbol, e.g. `BTCUSDT`, `ETHBTC` (a slash, dash or underscore between the assets is accepted).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Levels per side: 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 (default), 500, 1000 or 5000.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Price statistics for one spot pair (or up to 100 with `symbols`): last price and quantity, open, high, low, previous close, price change and percent, weighted average price, best bid/ask with sizes (24h only), base and quote volume, trade count, window open/close times and first/last trade ids. `window` switches from the 24 h statistics to a rolling window of 1-59 minutes, 1-23 hours or 1-7 days. With `market=usdm` or `market=coinm`, the same statistics for futures contracts.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-ticker

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required unless `symbols` is given.

parameters.name: symbols
parameters.description: Up to 100 comma-separated pairs, e.g. `BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT`; the answer is `items`.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: `24h` (default) or a rolling window: `1m`-`59m`, `1h`-`23h`, `1d`-`7d`, e.g. `4h`.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: `spot` (default), `usdm` (USDⓈ-M perpetual and delivery futures; `futures` also works) or `coinm` (COIN-M futures, e.g. `BTCUSD` or `BTCUSD_PERP`). Futures answers have 24h statistics only (no rolling `window`, no best bid/ask) and add `market`, `pair` and `base_volume`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Recent trades of a spot pair (id, price, quantity, quote quantity, time, taker side). With `aggregate=1`, aggregated trades instead (fills at one price and time merged), which can be filtered by `start`/`end` (at most 1 hour apart) or walked from `from_id`; pass `next_from_id` back as `from_id`; null when no more.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/binance-trades

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair symbol, e.g. `BTCUSDT`, `ETHBTC` (a slash, dash or underscore between the assets is accepted).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Trades per call, 1-1000 (default 500).

parameters.name: aggregate
parameters.description: true for aggregated trades (enables start, end, from_id).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Aggregated trades from this time (ISO or unix).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Aggregated trades until this time (ISO or unix); at most 1 hour after start.

parameters.name: from_id
parameters.description: Aggregated trade id to start from.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
